description: Checked-in Honeycomb query specifications for the three D3 product SLIs (session-create success split Rejected/Failed, launch-selection validity by code, time to first output), per the Overnight Execution Spec and Observability Context section 4. Source fields verified 2026-08-21 by reading anyharness/crates/proliferate-diagnostics-client/src/lifecycle.rs and anyharness/crates/proliferate-diagnostics-collector/src/export/otlp.rs on origin/observability/lane-b-stage-0-lifecycle-records (PR #2180, Lane B Stage 0, unmerged). [unverified against a live Honeycomb API]: never applied. Blocked on two independent things: (1) HONEYCOMB_READ_KEY returns 401 'unknown API key' as of 2026-08-21 (confirmed live, Lane A's item, not fixed by this lane); (2) Lane B has not yet posted a Stage-1 dogfood proof note (dataset + record shapes) to the Accounts and Wiring State doc as of this writing, so the anyharness dataset has no Stage-0 records in it yet. `apply`/`verify` tooling for this file does not exist yet -- writing the tooling was not useful before there was a credential to apply it with.

slis.title: Session-create success rate, split Rejected vs Failed
slis.status: buildable now: source record fully specified and emitted by PR #2180. Blocked only on (1) and (2) above, not on any missing instrumentation.

sourceRecord.recordShape: CanonicalLifecycleV1, phase=Terminal, outcome in {succeeded, rejected, failed, abandoned}

attributeNames.errorClassification: proliferate.error_classification (one of: workspace_not_found, workspace_single_session, session_id_conflict, launch_options_unavailable, launch_value_unsupported, agent_env_override_unsupported, route_auth_refused, invalid_request, internal_error)

slis.formula: failed_rate = COUNT(outcome=failed terminal records) / COUNT(all terminal records) over the window; rejected_rate is the same shape with outcome=rejected. Rejected is user-fixable and belongs in a digest; Failed is an engineering problem and is the one that can page (Observability Context section 4.2).
slis.threshold: [unverified, starting point only] Failed rate > 2% over a 15m window with a minimum of 20 terminal records in the window (to avoid alerting on noise at low volume). Recalibrate against the real Stage-1 baseline the first time this has a day of real dogfood or production data -- this number is not derived from any observed distribution, it is a placeholder consistent with the sign-in SLI's shape.

honeycombQuery.note: Honeycomb Query Specification shape (POST /1/queries/{dataset}). [unverified against the live API]

slis.runbookStub: When Failed rate rises: pull terminal anyharness.session.create records with outcome=failed for the window, group by proliferate.error_classification. internal_error dominating points at a runtime defect (engineering page); a spike concentrated in one of the other closed classifications (e.g. workspace_not_found, route_auth_refused) usually means a client/config issue that should have been Rejected, not Failed -- check create_lifecycle.rs's Rejected-vs-Failed classification logic for a possible misclassification bug before paging further.

slis.title: Launch-selection validity by bounded code
slis.status: BLOCKED on missing instrumentation, not just missing data. session.launch_selection.validated exists today only as a tracing::info! call site (create.rs, accepted arm and rejected arm), which the diagnostics tracing layer converts to a record_class=detailed record (DetailedKindV1::Log), never lifecycle (Observability Context section 4.1, 4.3; Spec - Lifecycle Export Pipe section 2). Verified 2026-08-21: PR #2180 (Lane B Stage 0) does not touch this event at all -- its own PR body lists exactly three operations instrumented (session.create, turn.execute, agent.start) and explicitly omits model.request with a stated reason; launch-selection promotion is not mentioned as in-scope or out-of-scope, it is simply not done. This matches the Context doc's own accounting: SLI #3 'needs promotion plus the pipe', distinct from SLIs #2 and #4 which only 'need Stage 0 plus the pipe'.
slis.whyThisMatters: A customer build's export is lifecycle-only by design (Spec - Lifecycle Export Pipe section 4-5: EXPORTED_CLASSES = LifecycleOnly). A detailed record never leaves a customer machine under any configuration. So even after Stage 2 ships, this SLI would still report zero production data forever unless the event is promoted from a tracing call to a genuine anyharness.* lifecycle catalog operation with its own closed safe-field list, the same treatment session.create/turn.execute/agent.start already got. Computing this SLI from the detailed record in the dogfood-only environment (which does export both classes) would technically produce a number, but it would be an internal-only proxy that silently stops working the day this ships to customers -- exactly the kind of proxy metric this program was told not to fake, so this lane is not building that workaround.

proposedSourceRecordIfPromoted.operationName: anyharness.session.launch_selection.validated (not yet a legal catalog name; would need adding to proliferate-diagnostics-protocol/src/v1/catalog.rs's closed P0 list first)
proposedSourceRecordIfPromoted.existingDetailedEventFields: result_code ("accepted" or a bounded rejected_key), counts, elapsed_ms -- create.rs:317-329 (accepted), :523-533 (rejected), per Observability Context section 4.1
proposedSourceRecordIfPromoted.formula: validity_rate = COUNT(result_code=accepted) / COUNT(all), broken down by rejected_key for the failure long tail

slis.threshold: not set -- cannot be set responsibly before the source record exists
slis.runbookStub: Not actionable yet. Once promoted: break down failures by rejected_key the same way the sign-in SLI breaks down by auth_sign_in_failure_code (guides/operating/production-alerts.md#sign-in-success-rate) -- one dominant rejected_key usually means a single upstream config or catalog problem, not a systemic one.
slis.followUp: File as a Rust follow-up (promote the tracing event to a lifecycle catalog operation, own safe-field list, own tests) -- out of Lane D's remit: it is a protocol/catalog change plus a call-site change in anyharness-lib, and Lane B holds the Rust build lock all night. Flagging as a concrete, cited contradiction rather than silently substituting a proxy.

slis.title: Time to first output (turn latency)
slis.status: BLOCKED on a missing numeric duration field, not on data or credentials. anyharness.turn.execute IS instrumented by PR #2180 (Started on begin_turn/ensure_open_turn, Terminal on turn_ended / commit_staged_prompt_terminal), but Observability Context's own phrasing, 'Started to Terminal duration', requires computing a delta between two separate log-shaped OTLP records that share proliferate.operation_id. Verified 2026-08-21 by reading the emitted record shape directly (otlp.rs, lifecycle.rs): there is no duration_ms (or any numeric elapsed-time) field anywhere on the Terminal record for turn.execute -- the only duration_ms in the whole lifecycle payload lives nested under lifecycle.model, which is never populated for this operation. turn.execute's safe_fields are exactly {stop_reason, engine_initiated}, neither numeric.
slis.whyThisMatters: Honeycomb computes per-event derived columns and per-event calculations; it does not join two arbitrary log rows by a shared attribute inside one query (that is a trace-span feature, and this export is OTLP logs, not spans with span.duration). Without a duration field on one row, 'Started to Terminal duration' is not computable from a single Honeycomb query against this record shape, full stop -- not a credentials problem, not a Stage-1 problem.
slis.proposedFix: Producer-side fix, not a Honeycomb-side one: attach the elapsed time the RAII guard already has in-process (it holds the Started instant and observes the Terminal transition) as a new safe-listed numeric argument on the Terminal record, e.g. duration_ms, added to anyharness.turn.execute's safe_fields in proliferate-diagnostics-client/src/lifecycle.rs. Once present, the SLI is a straight HEATMAP/P95 calculation.
slis.formulaOnceFixed: P50/P95/P99 of duration_ms where proliferate.name="anyharness.turn.execute", proliferate.lifecycle.phase="terminal", proliferate.lifecycle.outcome="succeeded" (successful turns only -- a rejected or failed turn did not produce real output, so including it would understate latency in a way that hides the metric that matters)
slis.threshold: not set -- propose a relative threshold (P95 > 1.5x its own trailing 24h baseline, sustained 15m) rather than an absolute number once real data exists, since acceptable turn latency varies enormously by model/provider and a fixed number would be arbitrary
slis.followUp: File as a Rust follow-up (add duration_ms to turn.execute's safe_fields, populate it at the Terminal call site) -- same remit boundary as launch-selection-validity above: Rust, Lane B's crate, build lock held all night.
